title: The card drill dance and Little White's house musicians
summary: Keppard describes the nine-part card drill in Economy Hall, then musicians at Little White's, including guitarist Stair Braddock.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: but who plays it though, Mr. Sire,

they can't get nobody to play it, and this car drill, it's got about nine parts to it, nine parts, the first thing that comes out, is grab your partner, grab your lady, grab your friend, then they're going to, start at the band, starts, bump, bump, bump, bump, bump, . hit the drum pair, boom. Then the ladies go and get their men and they all get in one line. And the men's on one side, the ladies on one side, and they're all in the whole hallway, in the economy hall. And that's where they started dancing. That's where they put that, uh, what they call a two-bar-four or three-bar-four and they dance according to what, what part they're going to put in. And on the last part, it goes in the six-eighth. That's the last part. Then after that, then everybody says, well, that's at 12 o'clock when they do that. Now, of course, the boys don't know anything about that. Now, now probably he's got one or two women like old man Glennie. Well, he heard about that. He knew all about it. He is a play with Joe Petit or the old-timers. But nevertheless, we're all old-timers. But, uh, who's that? You didn't know anything, Mr. Petit. That's all right. So, I said, why? Come in. You want the service. Come in. Come in. Come in. So, we're finished, Daniel. I take, and I says, well, we're going to take and we're going to all join together. Black Bunny, he used to take and hit them bass drums like nobody's business in the brass man. Now, they had this fella here, they call him Moran. He was playing cornet. Then after what comes the next week, the first one was the, what the, Jerry Blossom's was, uh, Harry Gougie. But he's in Chicago. He's a teacher. Well, that was the olden times. That's when the choir were made up a band of, um, now, if, now Mr. Roussel, if you're going to find on out of the street who was playing different places from a few clothes, Tom Madison, Little White. Well, Stair Brad was playing at Little White. You know what I'm talking about, Little White? Yes. Yes. Well, Little White, she used to be, uh, they are, they are, they are, they are between customers and them. Well, Stair Brad used to play, uh, uh, Madeline. And they had another, two other, uh, colorpuller and Willie. They had two white and they had a colorpuller and a colorpuller used to play, uh, one played guitar and the other played two of them played guitar and the other played a mammalian. See? And they used to play for the little white. Now, they never had no band, but there's that tree boy used to play that. Some of them was like a Mexican, but of course he died, Stair Braddock, I guess he's dead too. He got blind. Stair Braddock. Stair Braddock. He used to sell newspapers on Cadillac Street. Well, he used to be a bad boy on Cadillac Street one time before he started playing music. Well, he owns a lot of houses and everything else they tell me. But nevertheless, he was guitar player, and Sonny used to play Madeline, and Willie. Willie, let me see. Willie, I just remember his other name, but he was another white boy. Two white boys and colorpullers. But the colorpullers look like a Mexican, you know? Well, them three, they used to be a little white player. Now, in case Mr. Bruce, I like in case you want to find out who is Ben playing at City City Place, I can explain you that if you decide.
